children: Sweden’s current account surplus widened to SEK 126.2 billion in the second quarter of 2026, from SEK 103.7 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier.

This marked the largest surplus since the first quarter of 2025, driven by a wider primary income surplus, which rose to SEK 100.9 billion from SEK 76.0 billion, reflecting higher investment returns (SEK 97.6 billion vs SEK 72.5 billion in Q2 2025).
The services deficit narrowed to SEK 14.0 billion from SEK 36.6 billion, as exports rose by SEK 31 billion, far outpacing the SEK 8.4 billion increase in imports.
On the other hand, the goods surplus narrowed to SEK 67.7 billion from SEK 86.5 billion, as imports increased by SEK 61.5 billion, exceeding the SEK 42.7 billion rise in exports.
The secondary income deficit also widened to SEK 28.4 billion from SEK 22.3 billion.

title: Sweden Posts Largest Current Account Surplus in Over a Year
